c0081dad96: Mural titled “Take Off” commissioned by property owner to add to the already colorful stretch of Chicago Avenue in Ukranian Village. The elephant is as a symbol of good luck. Also, a nod to Save The Elephant.
d7847a5d16: The large, grinning green face of a fun creature looks out happily over Ashland Avenue from above Carnicerias Guanajuato. The mural is painted on the south-facing brick wall of 1440 N Ashland Ave and is the creation of Chicago artist Frank Quintero.
df03039036: A bouquet of flowers including peonies, rudbeckia, echinacea, tulips, coreopsis, flowering dogwood, and a swallowtail butterfly.
6c4ef67256: Dosmil is a Mexican street artist, born in Morelia, Michoacán. He has dedicated his work to the appropriation of urban spaces through the mural since 2015. With a varied and eclectic style, he represents through Mexican folklore an iconic character of his work, a personal reinterpretation of the torito de petate dance, one of the most traditional emblems of Morelia.
41b63e4e96: An enormous spider steps through the frame and into the alley. Inspired by the love of all creatures we share the neighborhood with, especially those less loved and sometimes maligned.
d55ed848f6: Arts Alive Chicago spearheaded this massive mural project on 35th street that included over 200 volunteers and community members painting Cyd Smillie’s designs. The north wall, “The Dream” traces the dreams of a baseball fan learning how to play the game, hit the winning homerun and celebrating with a parade. This mural includes images of local architectural landmarks, the Sox mascot and long time organ player and many others.
93c0e09536: White background with line drawings of a house, church, people and large words that say "Welcome to Buena Park"
